Very Hot, but Very Safe? Body protection for Tropics

I've ridden in sustained temps from about 10F to the 110'sF, both with and without humidity. Over about 90deg, it's more comfortable to have an insulating layer to keep the hot air OUT.

So, tropics and a riding vacation is the same gear as under 60F. For me that's an Aerostich 1-piece, boots, gloves, helmet with a shower at the end of the riding day.

Thanks for the reply.

Is an Aerostich 1-piece more suited for a day of total and utter riding, rather than a day of bike to the cafe, bike to the restaurant, bike to the beach, bike to the bar, bike home? What would you wear in those circumstances?

Also, the bike could be anything from a 100cc scooter, the sort of thing available in most foreign rental places.

That's why I qualified it with "riding vacation". I don't take a vacation and rent a scooter for short trips, I either have a car or stay someplace walkable and rely on taxi/public transportation for those few things where walking isn't an option. Of course I may be in a completely different situation of life than you, I travel with a wife, have been riding for decades already, have the means to stay where there's not a lot of reason to leave (for reference my last beach vacation was in Dec to Barbados, we rented a house on the beach with a grocery store/rum shop across the street, not a lot of reason to leave as we're not going out to drink/party/get food). Old people stuff.. :) Plus, I like to get my drink on while vacationing, which rules out motor vehicle operation...

But for what you're asking, I'd still be looking for a 1-piece riding suit that had armor in the knees, elbows, back, etc... that way you can just step into/out of it, run a cable lock through the sleeve and leave it with the scoot while wearing anything under it, including just a swimsuit. The feet would be the hard one for me to reconcile, feet and ankles are some of the most commonly broken/damaged body parts and nothing would suck more than not being able to walk after spending money to go on an island vacation.

It's just personal risk assessment though. 15 years ago I rented a scooter and tooled around with my wife (before we were married) in a small coastal town without using any gear. I wasn't really happy making that decision and shudder now that I think about it, but it was obviously an acceptable risk at that time. You'll have to do the same risk assessment. Just keep in mind that Impact protection will be nearly worthless in a crash (pads), it's Abrasion protection you're looking for. And to have that, you must be fully covered. Not much you can do to protect against breaking bones other than ankles (good boots), other than stay sober and alert.

Think about why you're going to whatever place. Is it to ride? Then take riding gear. Is it to do the beach/drinking/party scene? Then skip riding completely. You probably won't spend much more by using taxis and public transportation (especially if you're traveling with others and split the costs). But that's just my opinion....
